title: WHAT KIND OF CONSUMABLE PRODUCT WOULD BE MINE?
content:
Owning a consumable product can mean three different things. You may make each unit yourself, have a manufacturer produce your version of an existing category, or develop something genuinely new.

The distinction is the same ownership question used for other physical products, but consumables add issues such as repeat production, shelf life, consistency, ingredients or materials, packaging, and replenishment.

ROUTE A: MAKE IT YOURSELF
The product exists because you or your business produces it. Depending on the category, production capacity, consistency, storage, shelf life, sanitation, labeling, and other requirements may become important.

ROUTE B: YOUR VERSION OF AN EXISTING CATEGORY
The category already exists, but you want a product under your brand or specifications. This might involve private label, white label, contract manufacturing, custom formulation, packaging, or other supplier arrangements.

ROUTE C: INVENT SOMETHING NEW
The product itself requires development because the concept, formulation, material, delivery method, or function is genuinely new. Feasibility and testing may need to come before branding.

CHOOSE THE UNCERTAINTY YOU ACTUALLY HAVE
If you already know how to make the product and want to produce it, choose Route A. If the category is established and you mainly need your version produced, choose Route B. If figuring out what the product should physically be is part of the invention, choose Route C.

MAKE IT MYSELF → PDF 23.
MY VERSION OF AN EXISTING CONSUMABLE → PDF 24.
A NEW CONSUMABLE INVENTION → PDF 25.

EXAMPLE: THREE PEOPLE WANT THEIR OWN TEA PRODUCT

One person blends and packages loose-leaf tea themselves. Their production process is part of the business.

Another wants a tea blend under their brand and works with an established tea company that can formulate or package a version for them. The category already exists; the task is defining and sourcing their version.

A third is developing a genuinely new delivery format that requires technical development and testing. Their uncertainty is invention.

All three can own the resulting offer. The route determines what they need to investigate next.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Choose PDF 23, 24, or 25 based on how the product would become yours.
